claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi matrix is homogeneous in its as-cast or conventionally processed state.
Controlled low-energy laser surface remelting of CoCrFeNi will create a nanocrystalline surface layer.
Controlled low-energy laser surface remelting will create a compositionally graded surface layer in CoCrFeNi.
The laser process can produce a nanocrystalline gradient layer approximately 10–20 μm thick.
An optimized post-treatment will enhance oxide adhesion on the laser-remelted surface.
The nanocrystalline surface structure will accelerate formation of a protective oxide film during sliding.
The engineered surface will maintain a durable and adaptive oxide film during sliding.
The protective oxide film will act as a solid lubricant.
The composition gradient will promote localized oxidation resistance.
The composition gradient will help the oxide film withstand thermal cycling and mechanical stresses.
The persistent adaptive oxide film will reduce adhesive wear and friction.
Laser-treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
Laser-treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased coefficient of friction at elevated temperatures.
Untreated CoCrFeNi typically exhibits accelerated wear at elevated temperatures.
The proposed performance benefit is expected in ambient air at sliding loads of approximately 10–20 N.
The adaptive-oxide-film mechanism is well supported in similar material systems.
Thermal spallation may degrade the oxide film during cyclic high-temperature sliding.
